# Pull Request

## The issue or feature being addressed

Fixes #3286.

Concurrent initialization of the same registry key can construct multiple pipelines while retaining only one. Discarded candidates currently retain resources and reload registrations.

Related: #2539. This fix preserves concurrent construction and the existing cached lookup behavior.

## Details on the issue fix or feature implementation

- Compare each newly constructed candidate with the pipeline returned by ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd.
- Clean up discarded candidates in both generic and non-generic registries.
- Reuse the existing asynchronous cleanup helper used during pipeline reloads, including DisposeFailed telemetry.
- Document the cleanup behavior and add 10 regression cases covering concurrency, reload registrations, disposal callbacks, and asynchronous disposal failures.

As with existing reload cleanup, asynchronous disposal starts without blocking the lookup, and registry shutdown does not await these background operations. Feedback on this approach is welcome.

Validation:
- All 10 new regression cases failed against the original implementation.
- With the fix, 793 Polly.Core tests passed on .NET 10.
- 794 Polly.Core tests passed on .NET Framework 4.8.1.
- Polly.Core built for all five configured target frameworks with zero warnings or errors.

No public API signatures or dependencies were changed. Benchmarks and mutation tests were not run.

## Confirm the following

- [x] I started this PR by branching from the head of the default branch
- [x] I have targeted the PR to merge into the default branch
- [x] I have included unit tests for the issue/feature
- [x] I have successfully run a local build
- [x] I have the experience and knowledge necessary to understand, review, and validate all content in this PR.
